actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal executive agencies, defense contractors, subcontractors, and specific optical transceiver suppliers.
dimensions.evidence: prohibit Federal procurement of certain optical transceivers

dimensions.assessment: Bans federal procurement of covered optical transceivers from specified foreign entities, impacting supply chains and requiring federal procurement adjustments.
dimensions.evidence: prohibitions under subsection (a), as they apply to covered optical transceivers, shall take effect five years after the date of the enactment

dimensions.assessment: Directs various federal departments to conduct analyses, assessments, and strategies regarding domestic production capacity and supply chain risks, with no direct spending total specified.
dimensions.evidence: Secretary of Commerce, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense... shall conduct an analysis of optical transceiver design and production capacity

dimensions.assessment: Amends the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 to expand federal procurement restrictions to optical transceivers.
dimensions.evidence: Section 5949 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023... is amended

dimensions.assessment: Imposes a ban taking effect in 5 years, along with annual reporting requirements extending for ten years.
dimensions.evidence: annually thereafter for ten years, the Federal Acquisition Security Council shall include in the annual report

missing_information: Total compliance and replacement costs for federal agencies and contractors
importance_detail.rationale: The bill prohibits federal procurement of certain Chinese optical transceivers and associated components for critical systems after a five-year transition period, affecting federal agencies and defense contractors.
